questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests
questions.question_en:
Which of the following letters is the 7th to the left of the 11th letter from the right end of the series?
(Left) A D F G W R W S F G B C S X A D G H J K L Y O R E D H K H (Right)
questions.explanation_en: Count the series: it has 29 letters (A D F G W R W S F G B C S X A D G H J K L Y O R E D H K H). The 11th letter from the right end is at position 29 − 11 + 1 = 19 from the left, which is J. The 7th letter to the left of position 19 is at position 19 − 7 = 12, which is C.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and balance the given equation.
19 * 23 * 221 * 17 * 89 * 361
questions.explanation_en: Try option 3: 19 × 23 + 221 ÷ 17 − 89 = 361. Apply BODMAS: 19 × 23 = 437 and 221 ÷ 17 = 13. Then 437 + 13 − 89 = 361, which equals the right-hand side, so the sequence ×, +, ÷, −, = balances the equation. The other options give values far from 361 (e.g. option 1: 19 ÷ 23 is a fraction).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and balance the following equation.
45 * 45 * 45 * 45 * 45 * 1979
questions.explanation_en: Try option 1: 45 + 45 ÷ 45 = 45 × 45 − 1979. Left side: 45 ÷ 45 = 1, so 45 + 1 = 46. Right side: 45 × 45 = 2025, and 2025 − 1979 = 46. Both sides equal 46, so the combination +, ÷, =, ×, − is correct. Option 2 gives 45 − 1 = 44 on the left but 45 + 45 × 1979 on the right, which is far larger.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: In the evening, before sunset, X is facing towards the right hand side of the direction where his shadow is falling. He then turns right and walk 20 m. Then, he turns right again and walks 10 m. Then, he turns left and walks 10 m, and then turning right, he walks 20 m. Then, he turns right again and walks 30 m. At what distance and in which direction is X now from the starting point?
questions.explanation_en: In the evening the sun is in the west, so a shadow falls towards the east. The right-hand side of east is south, so X initially faces south. Turn right → west, walk 20 m; turn right → north, walk 10 m; turn left → west, walk 10 m; turn right → north, walk 20 m; turn right → east, walk 30 m. Net east-west movement: 20 + 10 west and 30 east = 0; net north movement: 10 + 20 = 30 m. So X is 30 m north of the start.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Study the given information, statement and conclusions carefully, and decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement.
P # Q means P is greater than Q.
P $ Q means P is either greater than or equal to Q.
P = Q means P is smaller than Q.
Statement:
C $ E, F # C, D = E.
Conclusions:
I. C # D
II. E # D

options.en: Both conclusions I and II follow
Either conclusion I or II follows

questions.explanation_en: Decode: C $ E means C ≥ E; F # C means F > C; D = E means D < E. Combining: F > C ≥ E > D. Conclusion I (C # D, i.e. C > D): since C ≥ E and E > D, C > D is definite — follows. Conclusion II (E # D, i.e. E > D): given directly — follows. Hence both conclusions follow.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Analogy & Classification
questions.question_en: Four number-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different.
questions.explanation_en: In each pair the second number is 4.5 times the first: 16 × 4.5 = 72, 24 × 4.5 = 108, 18 × 4.5 = 81. For 22, 22 × 4.5 = 99, but the pair gives 97, so 22 − 97 does not follow the pattern and is the odd one out.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
What approximate value should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?
23.87 ÷ 12.19 – 76.69 ÷ 29.89 × 17.37 = ?
questions.explanation_en: Round off the numbers: 23.87 ÷ 12.19 ≈ 24 ÷ 12 = 2; 76.69 ÷ 29.89 ≈ 77 ÷ 30 ≈ 2.57; 2.57 × 17.37 ≈ 44.6. As printed, 2 − 44.6 ≈ −43, which matches no option, so an operator has evidently been misprinted in the paper. The official key is 435; a form such as 23.87 × 17.37 + 12.19 … ≈ 415 + 12 + … lands near 435, so treat the official key as the reference. Note: question appears garbled; the method (round each number, then apply BODMAS) is what matters.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: In a row of a picture hall where all are facing north, Khalid is 25th from the left end and Kapil is 29th from the right end. They interchange their seats, and Sham who is sitting 34th from the left end is sitting at the 5th place to the left of Khalid new position. How many persons are there in one row of the picture hall?
questions.explanation_en: After the interchange, Khalid occupies Kapil's old seat, which is 29th from the right. Sham is 34th from the left and sits 5 places to the left of Khalid, so Khalid's new seat is 34 + 5 = 39th from the left. Total persons = (position from left) + (position from right) − 1 = 39 + 29 − 1 = 67.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Analogy & Classification
questions.question_en: Four number-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different.
questions.explanation_en: In every pair the second number is 3 times the first (13 × 3 = 39, 27 × 3 = 81, 23 × 3 = 69, 17 × 3 = 51), so the multiplication rule alone does not separate them. Look at the first numbers: 13, 23 and 17 are prime numbers, whereas 27 is composite (3 × 9). Hence 27 − 81 is the odd pair.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.
Statements:
A. Some dogs are goats.
B. All goats are peacocks.
C. All peacocks are eagles.
Conclusions:
I. Some peacocks are dogs.
II. All dogs are peacocks.
III. All eagles are peacocks.

options.en: Only conclusions II and III follow
Only conclusions I and II follow
All the conclusions, I, II and III, follow

questions.explanation_en: Draw the Venn picture: dogs partly overlap goats; goats sit entirely inside peacocks; peacocks sit entirely inside eagles. Conclusion I (some peacocks are dogs): the dogs that are goats are also peacocks — follows. Conclusion II (all dogs are peacocks): only some dogs are goats, so not definite — does not follow. Conclusion III (all eagles are peacocks): the statement is the reverse (all peacocks are eagles) — does not follow. Only I follows.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: In a row of 80 students, Ram is at the 15th position to the right of Rohit, who is at the 40th position from the right end. What will be the position of Ram from the left end?
questions.explanation_en: Rohit is 40th from the right in a row of 80, so from the left he is 80 − 40 + 1 = 41st. Ram is 15 places to his right (i.e. further from the left end), so Ram's position from the left = 41 + 15 = 56th.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en:
If
P # Q means P is the brother of Q,
P @ Q means P is the father of Q, and
P & Q means P is the sister of Q,
then how is A related to E in the expression A # B @ C & D # E?
questions.explanation_en: Decode A # B @ C & D # E: A is the brother of B; B is the father of C; C is the sister of D; D is the brother of E. So B is the father of C, D and E (they are siblings). A is the brother of B, i.e. brother of E's father — A is E's paternal uncle.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests
questions.question_en:
AOPQRSTUVDEFMNWXBZGHIJKLYC
How many letters in the above string occupy the same position as they occupy in the English alphabet?
questions.explanation_en: Compare each letter's place in the string with its alphabet number. A is at position 1 (A = 1) ✓. M is at position 13 (M = 13) ✓, N at position 14 (N = 14) ✓, and Y at position 25 (Y = 25) ✓. No other letter matches (e.g. O at 2, D at 10, C at 26). So four letters — A, M, N, Y — occupy their natural alphabetical positions.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
A statement is given, followed by two courses of action numbered I and II. You have to assume everything in the statement to be true, and on the basis of the information given in the statement, decide which of the suggested courses of action logically follow(s) for pursuing.
Statement:
False cases on dowry are on the increase in the last few years.
Courses of Action:
I. Government should instruct the local police administration to properly verify dowry complaints before registering an FIR.
II. Local police should take strict action on false cases of dowry.
questions.explanation_en: The problem is the rise in false dowry cases. Course I (proper verification of complaints before FIR) directly prevents false cases from being registered — it follows. Course II (strict action against those filing false cases) acts as a deterrent and is a practical, legal measure — it also follows. As both address the problem, the official key is that both I and II follow.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en:
If
A + B means A is the brother of B,
A − B means A is the sister of B and
A × B means A is the father of B,
then how is P related to S in the expression 'P × Q − R + S'?

options.en: P is the father of S
P is the son of S
P is the brother of S
P is the uncle of S

questions.explanation_en: P × Q: P is the father of Q. Q − R: Q is the sister of R. R + S: R is the brother of S. So Q, R and S are siblings, all children of P, which makes P the father of S.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Read the given statement and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statement is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement.
Statement:
Health is the best wealth of an individual.
Conclusions:
I. People do not think too much about health while making efforts to earn.
II. Wealth is of no use without health.

options.en: Either conclusion I or II follows.

questions.explanation_en: The statement says health matters more than wealth. Such advice is usually given because people tend to neglect health while chasing money, so conclusion I is accepted as implied. Conclusion II goes too far: calling health the 'best' wealth does not mean wealth is of 'no use' without it. Hence only conclusion I follows (as per the official key).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct?
105 ÷ 21 + 67 − 64 × 16 = 287
questions.explanation_en: Swap × and +: 105 ÷ 21 × 67 − 64 + 16. By BODMAS: 105 ÷ 21 = 5, then 5 × 67 = 335, then 335 − 64 + 16 = 287, which equals the right-hand side.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests
questions.question_en:
ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ
If the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 8th, 12th, 15th and 18th letters of the English alphabet (given above) are chosen to form a meaningful word (name of a disease), which letter will come in the middle of all? Each letter must be used and only once.
questions.explanation_en: The chosen letters are A(1), C(3), E(5), H(8), L(12), O(15) and R(18). They form the disease name CHOLERA. The word has 7 letters, so the middle (4th) letter is L.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Analogy & Classification
questions.question_en: Four letter-cluster pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different.
questions.explanation_en: In options 1, 3 and 4 the letters change alternately by +2 and −1 (e.g. INSPIRING: I+2=K, N−1=M, S+2=U, P−1=O …; ABANDONED: A+2=C, B−1=A …). In CABALETTA : ABZBJFRUY the pattern is reversed, −2 and +1 (C−2=A, A+1=B, B−2=Z, A+1=B …). So option 2 is the odd one.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Ramesh secured the 15th position from the top and is just 3 positions behind of his best friend Arvind in a class of 50 students. What will be the rank of Arvind from the bottom?
questions.explanation_en: Ramesh is 15th from the top and 3 places behind Arvind, so Arvind is 15 − 3 = 12th from the top. Rank from bottom = total − rank from top + 1 = 50 − 12 + 1 = 39th.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Analogy & Classification
questions.question_en: Four number-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different.
questions.explanation_en: In each pair the second number is 5 times the first: 55 × 5 = 275, 35 × 5 = 175 and 25 × 5 = 125. But 45 × 5 = 225, not 235, so 45-235 is the odd one.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and balance the given equation.
37 * 42 * 21 * 37 * 67 * 44
questions.explanation_en: Try option 4: 37 + 42 ÷ 21 × 37 − 67 = 44. By BODMAS, 42 ÷ 21 = 2, then 2 × 37 = 74, then 37 + 74 − 67 = 44. Both sides are equal, so the sign sequence +, ÷, ×, −, = balances the equation.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
A question is given followed by two statements labelled I and II. Identify which of the statements is/are sufficient to answer the question.
Question: Who is the shortest of all?
Statements:
I. Sachin is taller than Mohan and shorter than Vipin.
II. Devika is shorter than Gangan.

options.en: Both the statements I and II are insufficient to answer the question.
Either statement I alone or statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question.
Statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question, while statement I alone is not sufficient to answer the question.
Statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question, while statement II alone is not sufficient to answer the question.

questions.explanation_en: Statement I gives only Mohan < Sachin < Vipin. Statement II gives only Devika < Gangan. There is no link between the two groups, so even together they cannot tell us who is shortest of all. Both statements are insufficient.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Read the given statement and courses of action carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statement is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given courses of action logically follow(s) from the statement.
Statement:
In the last few years, the condition of roads in the state has continuously deteriorated.
Courses of Action:
I. State Government should take strict action against all the employees of Road Development Authority.
II. State Government should instruct Road Development Authorities to take regular inspection and necessary action to maintain roads.
questions.explanation_en: Course II is a practical step that tackles the problem through regular inspection and maintenance of roads. Course I is too harsh and unfair: punishing every employee without fixing responsibility is not a sensible remedy. So only II follows.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests
questions.question_en:
How many even numbers are immediately followed by an odd number but not immediately preceded by an even number in the following series?
3 4 3 2 5 6 7 4 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 6 5 4 3 2 2 4 5 6 7 8 9 9 7 6 0 7 6 5 4 3
questions.explanation_en: Scan each even number and check two things: the next number is odd and the previous number is not even. The qualifying ones are the 4 (2nd), 2 (4th), 6 (6th), 4 (8th), 4 (10th), 6 (12th), 8 (14th), 6 (16th), 4 (18th), 6 (24th), 8 (26th), 6 (33rd) and 4 (35th). Cases like '2 4 5' and '6 0 7' fail because the even number is preceded by an even number. Total = 13.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
What approximate value should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?
56.43 ÷ 27.89 − 67.78 + 98.19 × 13.67 = ?
questions.explanation_en: Round to the nearest whole numbers: 56 ÷ 28 − 68 + 98 × 14 = 2 − 68 + 1372 = 1306. (Exact working gives about 1276, and 1306 is still the nearest option.)

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: In the early morning after sunrise, the football coach of Argentina is discussing the strategies for the next match with Messi on the ground such that the coach's shadow falls exactly in front of Messi. In which direction is Messi facing?
questions.explanation_en: Just after sunrise the sun is in the east, so shadows fall towards the west. The coach's shadow falls westward and lies in front of Messi, so Messi stands west of the coach and faces him, i.e. Messi faces East.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: There are six persons, P, Q, R, S, T and U. T is older than no one. S is older than P. Q is younger than P. U is older than T but younger than Q. S is older than R. Who is the third youngest among all?
questions.explanation_en: T is older than no one, so T is the youngest. U is older than T but younger than Q, so U is second youngest in the intended order. From S > P > Q and S > R, the order taken is S > R/P > Q > U > T, which makes Q the third youngest (as per the official key).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Analogy & Classification
questions.question_en:
Select the option with the second term related to the first term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term in the given pair.
MATTER: BNUUSF
questions.explanation_en: MATTER: shift each letter +1 to get NBUUFS, then swap each pair of letters (NB→BN, UU→UU, FS→SF) to get BNUUSF. HOTELS +1 = IPUFMT; swapping pairs (IP→PI, UF→FU, MT→TM) gives PIFUTM.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Which two signs should be interchanged to make the following equation correct?
56 − 74 × 17 + 391 ÷ 23 = 1297
questions.explanation_en: Swap + and −: 56 + 74 × 17 − 391 ÷ 23. By BODMAS: 74 × 17 = 1258 and 391 ÷ 23 = 17. Then 56 + 1258 − 17 = 1297, which equals the right-hand side.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests
questions.question_en:
Select the term from among the given options that can replace the question mark (?) in the following series.
PMT, QOW, RQZ, SSC, ?
questions.explanation_en: Treat each letter position as its own series. First letters P, Q, R, S, T (+1); second letters M, O, Q, S, U (+2); third letters T, W, Z, C, F (+3, wrapping from Z to C). The next term is TUF.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en:
A person placed the 9 letters from A to I of the English alphabet into a row such that
• There is exactly two letters' gap between two vowels.
• I and B are placed at the extreme ends.
• D and F are placed between A and E.
• C is placed to the right of B and second to the left of D.
• E is placed exactly between A and I.
Which letter is placed in the middle of the row?
questions.explanation_en: C must be to the right of B, so B is at the left end (position 1) and I at the right end (9). E is midway between A and I with two letters between each vowel, so E is at 6 and A at 3. D and F lie between A and E (positions 4 and 5), and C is second to the left of D, so C = 2 and D = 4, F = 5. The row is B C A D F E _ _ I, and the middle (5th) letter is F.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Read the given statement and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statement is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statement.
Statement:
Physical exercises are good for health.
Conclusions:
I. Mostly players are healthy because of the involvement of physical exercise in their profession.
II. Ravinder played tennis at the age of 70.

options.en: Both conclusions I and II follow.
Either conclusion I or II follows.

questions.explanation_en: If physical exercise is good for health, then players, whose profession involves regular exercise, are likely to be healthy, so conclusion I follows. Conclusion II is about one particular person (Ravinder) and has no link to the statement. Only I follows.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
A statement is given followed by two arguments. Decide which of the arguments is/are strong with respect to the statement.
Statement:
Should a college run any course without seeking affiliation from the university?
Arguments:
I. Yes, it will provide more opportunities to individuals.
II. No, it will deteriorate the quality as college may not have all the equipment and resource to run any course.

options.en: Both arguments I and II are strong.
Neither argument I nor argument II is strong.

questions.explanation_en: Argument I is vague: unaffiliated courses do not create real opportunities, because their degrees are not recognised. Argument II rests on an assumption (that the college lacks equipment and resources) rather than on the actual purpose of affiliation, which is academic recognition and standards. As per the official key, neither argument is strong.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Analogy & Classification
questions.question_en: Four number-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different.
questions.explanation_en: In each pair the second number is 7 times the first: 59 × 7 = 413, 61 × 7 = 427 and 47 × 7 = 329. But 37 × 7 = 259, not 269, so 37-269 is the odd one.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
What approximate value should come in place of the question mark (?) in the following equation?
78.69 ÷ 29.19 × 13.17 − 45.67 ÷ 22.89 = ?
questions.explanation_en: The key's value 454 comes from reading the first operator as '+': 79 + 29 × 13 − 46 ÷ 23 = 79 + 377 − 2 = 454. As printed (78.69 ÷ 29.19 × 13.17 − 45.67 ÷ 22.89), the expression gives only about 2.7 × 13.17 − 2 ≈ 34, which matches no option.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Analogy & Classification
questions.question_en:
Select the option where the second word is related to the first word in the same way as the second word is related to the first word in the given pair.
IMAGINE: BLJGFMJ
questions.explanation_en: Rule from IMAGINE: split it as IMA | G | INE. Change each 3-letter block by +1, −1, +1 and reverse it (IMA → JLB → BLJ; INE → JMF → FMJ), keeping the middle letter G. Apply it to COLLEGE: COL → DNM → MND, L stays, EGE → FFF → FFF, giving MNDLFFF. The other options break the rule (e.g. SUCCESS should be DTTCTRF, not DTTCTRE).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: In a row of 50 students, Kajal is 8th to the left of Rashmi. If Rashmi is 25th from the left end of the row, what will be the position of Kajal from the right end of the row?
questions.explanation_en: Rashmi is 25th from the left and Kajal is 8 places to her left, so Kajal is 25 − 8 = 17th from the left. Position from the right = 50 − 17 + 1 = 34th.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
A question is given, followed by two statements labelled I and II. Identify which of the statements is/are sufficient to answer the question.
Question:
What will be the code of 'HUMAN' in the same language?
Statements:
I. 'FAHAD' is coded as '61814'.
II. 'WATER' is coded as '23120518'.

options.en: Information in both the statements I and II is necessary to answer the question.
Information in statement I alone is sufficient to answer the question, while information in statement II alone is not sufficient to answer the question.
Information in either statement I alone or statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question.
Information in statement II alone is sufficient to answer the question, while information in statement I alone is not sufficient to answer the question.

questions.explanation_en: Statement I: FAHAD → 6 1 8 1 4, i.e. each letter is replaced by its alphabet position. Statement II: WATER → 23 1 20 5 18, which shows the same rule. Either statement alone reveals the rule, giving HUMAN = 8 21 13 1 14 (82113114). So either statement alone is sufficient.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Analogy & Classification
questions.question_en: Four letter-cluster pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different.
questions.explanation_en: Rule: split the word into 3 letters + middle letter + 3 letters; change each block by +1, −1, +1 and reverse it, keeping the middle letter. IMAGINE → BLJGFMJ, SUCCESS → DTTCTRF and COLLEGE → MNDLFFF follow it. For COMMAND, AND → BME → EMB, so the code should be NNDMEMB, not NNDMENB. Option 3 is the odd one.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Select the correct combination of mathematical signs that can sequentially replace the * signs and balance the given equation.
34 * 69 * 23 * 37 * 23 * 882
questions.explanation_en: Try option 3: 34 − 69 ÷ 23 + 37 × 23 = 882. By BODMAS: 69 ÷ 23 = 3 and 37 × 23 = 851. Then 34 − 3 + 851 = 882, which balances the equation.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Analogy & Classification
questions.question_en: Four letter-cluster pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different.
questions.explanation_en: Rule: shift each letter by +1, then swap each adjacent pair. HOTELS → IPUFMT → PIFUTM; MATTER → NBUUFS → BNUUSF; ACTING → BDUJOH → DBJUHO. ACTUAL → BDUVBM → DBVUMB, but the given code is DBUVMB, so option 4 is the odd one.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Analogy & Classification
questions.question_en: Four number-pairs have been given, out of which three are alike in some manner and one is different. Select the one that is different.
questions.explanation_en: The rule is second = 3 × first + 2: 19 × 3 + 2 = 59, 17 × 3 + 2 = 53 and 23 × 3 + 2 = 71. But 29 × 3 + 2 = 89, not 91, so 29-91 is the odd one.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: There are six persons, P, Q, R, S, T and U. R is lighter than P but heavier than Q. S is lighter than U. T is heavier than P. U is lighter than Q. Who is the heaviest among them all?
questions.explanation_en: From the clues: Q < R < P, P < T, U < Q and S < U. Combined, S < U < Q < R < P < T, so T is the heaviest.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests
questions.question_en:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.
NRCH, IYNJ, FJUE, AQFB, ?
questions.explanation_en: Check each letter position. 1st letters N, I, F, A go −5, −3, −5, so the next is −3: X. 2nd letters R, Y, J, Q go +7, +11, +7, so the next is +11: B. 3rd letters C, N, U, F go +11, +7, +11, so the next is +7: M. Only XBMW starts with XBM (its 4th letter W continues H, J, E, B with a −5 step).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Analogy & Classification
questions.question_en: In the following, select the odd letter/letters from the given alternatives.
questions.explanation_en: MKH (13→11→8), WUR (23→21→18) and KIF (11→9→6) all step backwards by −2 and then −3. MPR (13→16→18) steps forwards by +3 and then +2, so it is the odd one.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests
questions.question_en: In a certain code language, 'STOPWARS' is written as 'POTSSRAW', 'LOGIPERT' is written as 'IGOLTREP'. What is the code for 'LAPTOPST' in that code language?
questions.explanation_en: The word is split into two halves of 4 letters and each half is reversed: STOP|WARS → POTS|SRAW and LOGI|PERT → IGOL|TREP. So LAPT|OPST → TPAL|TSPO = TPALTSPO.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
A statement is followed by a set of conclusions in the given question. Identify which conclusion follows logically from the following statement.
Statement:
Raveena goes to the gym daily, as her father has advised her to exercise.
Conclusion:
I. Raveena's father cares for her daughter health.
II. Raveena is suffering from some chronic disease.
questions.explanation_en: The father advising daily exercise shows that he cares about his daughter's health, so conclusion I follows. Nothing in the statement suggests any disease (people exercise to stay fit), so conclusion II does not follow. Only I follows.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en: If '÷' means '×', '–' means '+', '×' means '÷' and '+' means '–', then 38 × 57 ÷ 9 – 18 + 12 = ?
questions.explanation_en: Replacing the signs gives 38 ÷ 57 × 9 + 18 − 12. By BODMAS: 38/57 = 2/3, then 2/3 × 9 = 6, then 6 + 18 − 12 = 12.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Analogy & Classification
questions.question_en:
Select that missing pair (Third number : Fourth number) which is related in the same way as the first number is related to the second number and fifth number is related to sixth number. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)
442 : 633 :: ? : ?  :: 186 : 377
questions.explanation_en: The second number is the first plus 191: 442 + 191 = 633 and 186 + 191 = 377. Checking the options, 313 + 191 = 504, so 313 : 504 fits. The others differ by 201, 181 and 190.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: P, Q, R, S, T, U and V are seven friends sitting in a single row facing North. S is to the immediate right of R. T and P are neighbors of U.Q is to the immediate left of R and on second place from left most end. P is at the right most end.Who is sitting on the immediate left of P?
questions.explanation_en: Q is 2nd from the left and immediately left of R, so R = 3 and S (immediately right of R) = 4. P is at the right end (7), and U, whose neighbours are T and P, is at 6 with T at 5. V takes position 1. The immediate left of P is U.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.
Statements:
I. Some C are D.
II. Some D are E.
III. No E is G.
Conclusion:
I. Some E are C.
II. No D is G.
III. Some G are C.
questions.explanation_en: 'Some C are D' and 'Some D are E' are two particular statements, so no definite link between C and E follows (I fails). 'No E is G' only separates the D that are E from G; other D may or may not be G (II fails). Nothing at all links G with C (III fails). Hence no conclusion follows.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Mona is 13th from the right end in a row of 40 girls. What is his position from the left end?
questions.explanation_en: Position from the left = total − position from the right + 1 = 40 − 13 + 1 = 28th.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests

In the following question, select the missing number from the given series.
200, 197, 206, 179, 260, ?
questions.explanation_en: The differences are −3, +9, −27, +81, i.e. powers of 3 with alternating signs. The next difference is −243, so the missing term = 260 − 243 = 17.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Analogy & Classification
questions.question_en: In the following, select the odd letter/letters from the given alternatives.
questions.explanation_en: WXUZ (23, 24, 21, 26), NOLQ (14, 15, 12, 17) and IJGL (9, 10, 7, 12) all follow +1, −3, +5. EFCG (5, 6, 3, 7) follows +1, −3, +4, so it is the odd one.

NQT : ORU :: ADH : ?
questions.explanation_en: Each letter of NQT moves +1 to give ORU. Applying +1 to ADH gives BEI.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: If A + B means 'A' is the husband of 'B', A – B means 'A' is the wife of 'B', A × B means 'A' is the mother of 'B', A ÷ B means 'A' is the son of 'B'. If J ÷ P + K × M – R, then How is P related to R?
questions.explanation_en: J ÷ P: J is the son of P. P + K: P is the husband of K. K × M: K is the mother of M, so P is M's father. M − R: M is the wife of R. So P is the father of R's wife, i.e. R's wife's father (father-in-law).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
By Interchanging the given two numbers which of the following equation will be not correct?
7 and 9
questions.explanation_en: Interchange 7 and 9 in each equation. (1) 7 − 9 + 3 = 1 ✓; (3) 7 × 1 − 9 × 2 = −11 ✓; (4) 9 × 2 + 7 − 4 = 21 ✓. But (2) becomes 7 × 4 − 9 × 3 = 28 − 27 = 1, not 4, so it is the equation that is not correct.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Analogy & Classification

6 : 180 :: 8 : 448 :: 10 : ?

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
In the given question, a statement is followed by two courses of action. Based on the information given in the statement, you have to assume everything in the statement to be true. Identify which course(s) of action logically follows.
Statement:
A bridge collapsed in town Y due to poor construction.
Course of Action:
I. Search-and-rescue operations should be conducted immediately.
II. People should leave town Y and move to town X.
questions.explanation_en: After a bridge collapse, the immediate need is to rescue people who may be trapped or injured, so course I follows. Asking people to leave the whole town is impractical and out of proportion to the problem, so course II does not follow.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
A statement is followed by a set of conclusions in the given question. Identify which conclusion follows logically from the following statement.
Statement:
For the past three years the ABC Corporation has been planning to expand its operations in order to reach out to the world market.
Conclusion:
I. The ABC corporation is not competitive.
II. The ABC corporation wants to capture the global market.
questions.explanation_en: Planning to expand operations to reach the world market shows that the corporation wants a global presence, so conclusion II follows. Nothing in the statement suggests it is uncompetitive; if anything it suggests the opposite. Only II follows.

325 : 512 :: ? : ? :: 148 : 335

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Analogy & Classification
questions.question_en: Thermometer : Temperature :: Barometer : ?
questions.explanation_en: Instrument : what it measures. A thermometer measures temperature; a barometer measures atmospheric pressure. Humidity is measured by a hygrometer, wind speed by an anemometer and rainfall by a rain gauge.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Analogy & Classification
questions.question_en: Bird : Aviary :: Bee : ?
questions.explanation_en: An aviary is a place where birds are kept; an apiary is a place where bees are kept. A kennel is for dogs, a stable for horses, and a burrow is a wild animal's hole.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Analogy & Classification
questions.question_en: Cobbler : Leather :: Carpenter : ?
questions.explanation_en: Worker : raw material. A cobbler works with leather; a carpenter works with wood. Furniture is the product and a saw is a tool, so they break the relation.

questions.explanation_en: Each letter moves 3 places forward: R→U, O→R, A→D, D→G. So S→V, W→Z, A→D, N→Q gives VZDQ.

questions.explanation_en: In each row, first ÷ second = third: 12 ÷ 4 = 3, 45 ÷ 9 = 5, so 56 ÷ ? = 7 gives ? = 8.

questions.explanation_en: The word is reversed and each letter is moved one step forward. FRUIT reversed = TIURF, +1 gives UJVSG. LEMON reversed = NOMEL, +1 gives OPNFM.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests
questions.question_en: In a code language, 'sky is blue' is written as 'ro mi ta', 'blue sea deep' as 'la mi su' and 'deep sky' as 'ta la'. What is the code for 'sea'?
questions.explanation_en: Common word in statements 2 and 3 is 'deep' = 'la'. Common word in 1 and 3 is 'sky' = 'ta'. Common in 1 and 2 is 'blue' = 'mi'. In statement 2 the remaining code 'su' stands for 'sea'.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests

questions.explanation_en: The 15th letter from the right is the 26 − 15 + 1 = 12th from the left, L. The 5th to its left is the 7th letter, G.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests

questions.explanation_en: Alphabetical order: D, E, H, I, L. The middle (third) letter is H.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests
questions.question_en: Which letter is the 8th to the right of the letter that is 5th to the left of M in the English alphabet?
questions.explanation_en: M is the 13th letter. 5th to its left is the 8th letter, H. 8th to the right of H is the 16th letter, P.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests
questions.question_en: How many letters of the English alphabet lie between the 8th letter from the left end and the 8th letter from the right end?
questions.explanation_en: The 8th from the left is H (8th). The 8th from the right is the 19th from the left, S. Letters between them = 19 − 8 − 1 = 10.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests
questions.question_en: If the letters of the word FRIEND are arranged in alphabetical order, how many letters remain in the same position as in the original word?
questions.explanation_en: FRIEND sorted is D, E, F, I, N, R. Comparing position by position with F, R, I, E, N, D, only the fifth letter (N) is unchanged.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests
questions.question_en: In the word STORM, how many pairs of letters are there such that the gap between their positions in the word equals the gap between their positions in the English alphabet?
questions.explanation_en: S(1)-T(2): word gap 1, alphabet gap 1. T(2)-R(4): word gap 2, alphabet gap 20 − 18 = 2. O(3)-M(5): word gap 2, alphabet gap 15 − 13 = 2. No other pair matches. Total 3.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests
questions.question_en: In a series of figures, the first figure has 1 line, the second has 3 lines, the third has 6 lines and the fourth has 10 lines. How many lines will the fifth figure have?
questions.explanation_en: The increments are +2, +3, +4, so the next increment is +5: 10 + 5 = 15 (triangular numbers).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests
questions.question_en: In a series of figures, each figure shows a letter and a number: A2, C4, F8, J16. What will the fifth figure show?
questions.explanation_en: Letters advance by +2, +3, +4, so next is +5: J → O. Numbers double: 16 × 2 = 32. Hence O32.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests
questions.question_en:
Matrix I (rows 0–4, columns 0–4):
Row 0: P E N T A
Row 1: E N T A P
Row 2: N T A P E
Row 3: T A P E N
Row 4: A P E N T
Matrix II (rows 5–9, columns 5–9):
Row 5: O R S I L
Row 6: R S I L O
Row 7: S I L O R
Row 8: I L O R S
Row 9: L O R S I
Each letter is coded by its row number followed by its column number (for example, P can be 00 or 14). Which set of numbers correctly represents the word PEARL?
questions.explanation_en: P = 00, E = 10, A = 22, R = 65, L = 77 are all correct. In the other sets 69 = O, 58 = I and 03 = T, so each has one wrong letter.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests
questions.question_en:
Matrix I (rows 0–4, columns 0–4):
Row 0: P E N T A
Row 1: E N T A P
Row 2: N T A P E
Row 3: T A P E N
Row 4: A P E N T
Matrix II (rows 5–9, columns 5–9):
Row 5: O R S I L
Row 6: R S I L O
Row 7: S I L O R
Row 8: I L O R S
Row 9: L O R S I
Each letter is coded by its row number followed by its column number (for example, P can be 00 or 14). Which set of numbers correctly represents the word STONE?
questions.explanation_en: S = 66, T = 30, O = 87, N = 20, E = 42. The first and third sets end with N (02, 11) instead of E; the fourth has 24 = E in place of N.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests
questions.question_en:
Matrix I (rows 0–4, columns 0–4):
Row 0: P E N T A
Row 1: E N T A P
Row 2: N T A P E
Row 3: T A P E N
Row 4: A P E N T
Matrix II (rows 5–9, columns 5–9):
Row 5: O R S I L
Row 6: R S I L O
Row 7: S I L O R
Row 8: I L O R S
Row 9: L O R S I
Each letter is coded by its row number followed by its column number (for example, P can be 00 or 14). The set 12, 99, 86, 33 represents which word?
questions.explanation_en: 12 = row 1, column 2 = T; 99 = I; 86 = L; 33 = E. So the word is TILE.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests
questions.question_en:
Matrix I (rows 0–4, columns 0–4):
Row 0: P E N T A
Row 1: E N T A P
Row 2: N T A P E
Row 3: T A P E N
Row 4: A P E N T
Matrix II (rows 5–9, columns 5–9):
Row 5: O R S I L
Row 6: R S I L O
Row 7: S I L O R
Row 8: I L O R S
Row 9: L O R S I
Each letter is coded by its row number followed by its column number (for example, P can be 00 or 14). Which of the following sets does NOT represent the word RAIN?
questions.explanation_en: In the third set 44 is row 4, column 4 = T, not N, so it spells RAIT. All other sets decode to R-A-I-N (e.g. 88 = R, 31 = A, 85 = I, 34 = N).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests
questions.question_en: In a 3 × 3 grid, Row 1 is A B C, Row 2 is D E F and Row 3 is G H I. Each letter is coded by its row number followed by its column number, so BAD is coded 12 11 21. What is the code for HIDE?
questions.explanation_en: H = row 3, column 2 = 32; I = 33; D = row 2, column 1 = 21; E = 22. Option 2 reverses row and column; option 4 uses G (31) for H.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests
questions.question_en: A 4 × 4 letter grid is: Row 1: P L A N; Row 2: T R E S; Row 3: M O U D; Row 4: C K I G. Each letter is coded by its COLUMN number followed by its ROW number. What is the code for MOUSE?
questions.explanation_en: M is in column 1, row 3 → 13; O → 23; U → 33; S is column 4, row 2 → 42; E is column 3, row 2 → 32. The first option uses row-then-column order, which is the trap.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Pointing to a photograph, Ravi says, 'She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son.' How is the girl related to Ravi?
questions.explanation_en: Ravi's grandfather's only son is Ravi's father. The daughter of Ravi's father is Ravi's sister.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: A is the sister of B. C is the mother of B. D is the father of C. How is A related to D?
questions.explanation_en: A and B are children of C. D is C's father, so A is D's granddaughter.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Pointing to a man, a woman says, 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the woman related to the man?
questions.explanation_en: The only daughter of the woman's mother is the woman herself. So the man's mother is the woman: she is his mother.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Pointing to a lady, Anil said, 'She is the wife of my mother's only brother.' How is the lady related to Anil?
questions.explanation_en: Anil's mother's only brother is his maternal uncle (Mama). The uncle's wife is Anil's Mami, i.e. maternal aunt.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: P is the father of Q. Q is the sister of R. R is the mother of S. How is P related to S?
questions.explanation_en: P is father of both Q and R. R is S's mother, so P is the father of S's mother: maternal grandfather.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: In a certain notation, A + B means A is the mother of B; A - B means A is the brother of B; A x B means A is the father of B. What does P - Q x R mean?

options.en: P is the paternal uncle of R
P is the maternal uncle of R
P is the father of R
P is the grandfather of R

questions.explanation_en: P - Q: P is the brother of Q. Q x R: Q is the father of R. So P is the brother of R's father: paternal uncle.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Pointing to a photograph, a man said, 'I have no brother or sister, but that man's father is my father's son.' Whose photograph was it?
questions.explanation_en: The man has no brother, so 'my father's son' is the man himself. Hence 'that man's father' is the speaker, so the photograph is of his son.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Pointing to a boy, Meena said, 'He is the son of my mother's only son.' How is the boy related to Meena?
questions.explanation_en: Meena's mother's only son is Meena's brother. The brother's son is Meena's nephew.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: A man walks 5 km east, turns left and walks 3 km, then turns left again and walks 5 km. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation_en: East 5, left turn faces north (3 km), left again faces west (5 km). The east and west movements cancel, leaving 3 km north of the start.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: A person walks 8 km north, then turns right and walks 6 km. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation_en: North 8 and east 6 form a right triangle. Distance = sqrt(8^2 + 6^2) = sqrt(100) = 10 km, and he lies to the north-east of the start.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Rahul faces east. He turns 90 degrees clockwise and then 135 degrees anticlockwise. In which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation_en: East turned 90 degrees clockwise is south. Turning 135 degrees anticlockwise from south passes east (90 degrees) and reaches north-east (a further 45 degrees).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: One morning after sunrise, Mohan stood facing a pole. The shadow of the pole fell on his right side. Which direction was he facing?
questions.explanation_en: In the morning the sun is in the east, so shadows fall towards the west. The shadow was on his right, so west was on his right — that happens only when he faces south (facing north, west would be on the left).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Ram walks 10 m south, turns left and walks 8 m, then turns left again and walks 4 m. How far is he from the starting point and in which direction?
questions.explanation_en: Take the start as (0, 0). South 10 gives (0, -10); left (east) 8 gives (8, -10); left (north) 4 gives (8, -6). Distance = sqrt(8^2 + 6^2) = 10 m, and the point lies south-east of the start.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Sunita is facing north-west. She turns 90 degrees clockwise and then 180 degrees anticlockwise. In which direction is she facing now?
questions.explanation_en: North-west turned 90 degrees clockwise is north-east. Turning 180 degrees from north-east gives the opposite direction, south-west.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: A is 5 m east of B. C is 5 m north of B. D is 5 m west of C. In which direction is D with respect to A?
questions.explanation_en: Take B at (0, 0): A = (5, 0), C = (0, 5), D = (-5, 5). D is 10 m west and 5 m north of A, so it lies north-west of A.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: A man walks 15 m towards the west, turns right and walks 12 m, turns right again and walks 15 m, then turns left and walks 6 m. How far is he from the starting point and in which direction?
questions.explanation_en: West 15 gives (-15, 0); right (north) 12 gives (-15, 12); right (east) 15 gives (0, 12); left (north) 6 gives (0, 18). The east-west displacement cancels, leaving 18 m due north.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: In the evening, just before sunset, Rekha and Sohan stand facing each other. Rekha's shadow falls exactly to her left. In which direction is Sohan facing?
questions.explanation_en: Before sunset the sun is in the west, so shadows fall to the east. East is on Rekha's left, so Rekha faces south. Sohan faces Rekha, so he faces north.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Rohan ranks 12th from the top in a class of 40 students. What is his rank from the bottom?
questions.explanation_en: Rank from bottom = total - rank from top + 1 = 40 - 12 + 1 = 29.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: In a row of girls, Neha is 7th from the left end and 12th from the right end. How many girls are there in the row?
questions.explanation_en: Total = 7 + 12 - 1 = 18 (Neha is counted in both ranks).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: In a row of 40 students, Aman is 14th from the left and Bharat is 18th from the right. How many students are between them?
questions.explanation_en: Bharat's position from the left = 40 - 18 + 1 = 23. Students between = 23 - 14 - 1 = 8.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: A is taller than B, B is taller than C, D is taller than A, and E is shorter than C. Who is the second tallest?
questions.explanation_en: The order is D > A > B > C > E. D is the tallest, so A is second tallest.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Raj is 9th from the top in a class. Amit is 14th from the bottom. If they exchange positions, Raj becomes 19th from the top. How many students are in the class?
questions.explanation_en: Raj now stands where Amit stood, so Amit's original position is 19th from the top and 14th from the bottom. Total = 19 + 14 - 1 = 32.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: P is heavier than Q but lighter than R. S is heavier than R. T is lighter than Q. Who is the second heaviest?
questions.explanation_en: Order from heaviest: S > R > P > Q > T. So R is second heaviest.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Kiran ranks 15th from the top and 25th from the bottom in a class. Divya ranks 7 places above Kiran. What is Divya's rank from the bottom?
questions.explanation_en: Total = 15 + 25 - 1 = 39. Divya's rank from top = 15 - 7 = 8. From the bottom = 39 - 8 + 1 = 32.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: In a row of children facing north, Asha is 18th from the left end and Bina is 21st from the right end. When they interchange their places, Asha becomes 26th from the left end. How many children are there in the row?
questions.explanation_en: After the exchange Asha stands at Bina's old place, so that place is 26th from the left and 21st from the right. Total = 26 + 21 − 1 = 46.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: In a class of 42 students, Tarun is 17th from the top and is 5 places below his friend Sameer. What is Sameer's rank from the bottom?
questions.explanation_en: Sameer is 5 places above Tarun: 17 − 5 = 12th from the top. From the bottom = 42 − 12 + 1 = 31st. 26th is Tarun's rank from the bottom.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Six friends J, K, L, M, N and O are of different ages. L is older than only O. J is older than K but younger than M. N is younger than K but older than L. Who is the third oldest?
questions.explanation_en: L is older than only O, so O is youngest and L second youngest. N > L, K > N, J > K and M > J give M > J > K > N > L > O. The third oldest is K.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G sit in a row facing north. C sits at the extreme left end and D at the extreme right end. E sits third to the right of C. B sits between E and G and is an immediate neighbour of both. G sits to the left of E. A sits to the immediate right of E. Who sits between A and D?
questions.explanation_en: C = 1 and D = 7. E is third to the right of C, so E = 4. G is left of E and B sits between them, so B = 3 and G = 2. A = 5 (immediate right of E), which leaves F = 6, the seat between A and D.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 3:30?

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand at 4:20?

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: At what time between 4 and 5 o'clock will the two hands of a clock coincide?
questions.explanation_en: Hands coincide when M = (60 × H) / 11 minutes past H. For H = 4: 240/11 = 21 9/11 minutes past 4.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: A watch gains 2 minutes every hour. It was set right at 6:00 a.m. on Monday. What time will it show at the true time of 6:00 p.m. on the same day?
questions.explanation_en: From 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. is 12 hours. Gain = 12 × 2 = 24 minutes, so the watch shows 6:24 p.m.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: On which day of the week did India become independent on 15 August 1947?
questions.explanation_en: Odd-day method: 1600 years = 0, next 300 years = 1, next 46 years (11 leap years) = 57 days = 1, so 1946 years = 2 odd days. Days from 1 Jan to 15 Aug 1947 = 227 = 3 odd days. Total 5 odd days, and 5 corresponds to Friday (0 = Sunday).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: If 26 January 2026 was a Monday, what day of the week was 15 August 2026?
questions.explanation_en: From 26 January to 15 August 2026 (a non-leap year): remaining days of January 5, February 28, March 31, April 30, May 31, June 30, July 31, plus 15 in August = 201 days. 201 = 28 × 7 + 5, so 5 days after Monday = Saturday.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: How many odd days are there in 200 years?
questions.explanation_en: 100 years have 5 odd days, so 200 years have 10 odd days = 10 − 7 = 3 odd days.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: An arrow initially points North. In step 1 it turns 45° clockwise, in step 2 it turns 90° clockwise, in step 3 it turns 135° clockwise, and in step 4 it turns 180° clockwise. In which direction does it point after step 4?
questions.explanation_en: Total rotation = 45 + 90 + 135 + 180 = 450° clockwise. 450 − 360 = 90° clockwise from North = East.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: A pointer initially points East. In each step it turns 90° anticlockwise. In which direction will it point after 5 steps?
questions.explanation_en: 5 × 90° = 450° anticlockwise. 450 − 360 = 90° anticlockwise from East, which is North.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: A wall clock shows 4:20. What time will its image in a plane mirror (placed vertically beside it) appear to show?
questions.explanation_en: Mirror time = 11:60 − actual time = 11:60 − 4:20 = 7:40.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: The mirror image of a clock shows the time as 9:15. What is the actual time?
questions.explanation_en: Actual time = 11:60 − mirror time = 11:60 − 9:15 = 2:45. The relation works both ways.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: For which of the following times does the mirror image of a clock show the same time as the actual time?
questions.explanation_en: 11:60 − 6:00 = 5:60 = 6:00, so 6:00 looks unchanged (both hands lie on the vertical axis). 3:00 appears as 9:00, 9:30 as 2:30 and 4:20 as 7:40.
