Row 9: L O R S I
Each letter is coded by its row number followed by its column number (for example, P can be 00 or 14). Which of the following sets does NOT represent the word RAIN?
questions.explanation_en: In the third set 44 is row 4, column 4 = T, not N, so it spells RAIT. All other sets decode to R-A-I-N (e.g. 88 = R, 31 = A, 85 = I, 34 = N).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests
questions.question_en: In a 3 × 3 grid, Row 1 is A B C, Row 2 is D E F and Row 3 is G H I. Each letter is coded by its row number followed by its column number, so BAD is coded 12 11 21. What is the code for HIDE?
questions.explanation_en: H = row 3, column 2 = 32; I = 33; D = row 2, column 1 = 21; E = 22. Option 2 reverses row and column; option 4 uses G (31) for H.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Series, Coding–Decoding & Alphabet Tests
questions.question_en: A 4 × 4 letter grid is: Row 1: P L A N; Row 2: T R E S; Row 3: M O U D; Row 4: C K I G. Each letter is coded by its COLUMN number followed by its ROW number. What is the code for MOUSE?
questions.explanation_en: M is in column 1, row 3 → 13; O → 23; U → 33; S is column 4, row 2 → 42; E is column 3, row 2 → 32. The first option uses row-then-column order, which is the trap.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Pointing to a photograph, Ravi says, 'She is the daughter of my grandfather's only son.' How is the girl related to Ravi?
questions.explanation_en: Ravi's grandfather's only son is Ravi's father. The daughter of Ravi's father is Ravi's sister.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: A is the sister of B. C is the mother of B. D is the father of C. How is A related to D?
questions.explanation_en: A and B are children of C. D is C's father, so A is D's granddaughter.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Pointing to a man, a woman says, 'His mother is the only daughter of my mother.' How is the woman related to the man?
questions.explanation_en: The only daughter of the woman's mother is the woman herself. So the man's mother is the woman: she is his mother.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Pointing to a lady, Anil said, 'She is the wife of my mother's only brother.' How is the lady related to Anil?
questions.explanation_en: Anil's mother's only brother is his maternal uncle (Mama). The uncle's wife is Anil's Mami, i.e. maternal aunt.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: P is the father of Q. Q is the sister of R. R is the mother of S. How is P related to S?
questions.explanation_en: P is father of both Q and R. R is S's mother, so P is the father of S's mother: maternal grandfather.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: In a certain notation, A + B means A is the mother of B; A - B means A is the brother of B; A x B means A is the father of B. What does P - Q x R mean?

options.en: P is the paternal uncle of R
P is the maternal uncle of R
P is the father of R
P is the grandfather of R

questions.explanation_en: P - Q: P is the brother of Q. Q x R: Q is the father of R. So P is the brother of R's father: paternal uncle.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Pointing to a photograph, a man said, 'I have no brother or sister, but that man's father is my father's son.' Whose photograph was it?
questions.explanation_en: The man has no brother, so 'my father's son' is the man himself. Hence 'that man's father' is the speaker, so the photograph is of his son.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Pointing to a boy, Meena said, 'He is the son of my mother's only son.' How is the boy related to Meena?
questions.explanation_en: Meena's mother's only son is Meena's brother. The brother's son is Meena's nephew.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: A man walks 5 km east, turns left and walks 3 km, then turns left again and walks 5 km. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation_en: East 5, left turn faces north (3 km), left again faces west (5 km). The east and west movements cancel, leaving 3 km north of the start.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: A person walks 8 km north, then turns right and walks 6 km. How far and in which direction is he from the starting point?
questions.explanation_en: North 8 and east 6 form a right triangle. Distance = sqrt(8^2 + 6^2) = sqrt(100) = 10 km, and he lies to the north-east of the start.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Rahul faces east. He turns 90 degrees clockwise and then 135 degrees anticlockwise. In which direction is he facing now?
questions.explanation_en: East turned 90 degrees clockwise is south. Turning 135 degrees anticlockwise from south passes east (90 degrees) and reaches north-east (a further 45 degrees).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: One morning after sunrise, Mohan stood facing a pole. The shadow of the pole fell on his right side. Which direction was he facing?
questions.explanation_en: In the morning the sun is in the east, so shadows fall towards the west. The shadow was on his right, so west was on his right — that happens only when he faces south (facing north, west would be on the left).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Ram walks 10 m south, turns left and walks 8 m, then turns left again and walks 4 m. How far is he from the starting point and in which direction?
questions.explanation_en: Take the start as (0, 0). South 10 gives (0, -10); left (east) 8 gives (8, -10); left (north) 4 gives (8, -6). Distance = sqrt(8^2 + 6^2) = 10 m, and the point lies south-east of the start.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Sunita is facing north-west. She turns 90 degrees clockwise and then 180 degrees anticlockwise. In which direction is she facing now?
questions.explanation_en: North-west turned 90 degrees clockwise is north-east. Turning 180 degrees from north-east gives the opposite direction, south-west.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: A is 5 m east of B. C is 5 m north of B. D is 5 m west of C. In which direction is D with respect to A?
questions.explanation_en: Take B at (0, 0): A = (5, 0), C = (0, 5), D = (-5, 5). D is 10 m west and 5 m north of A, so it lies north-west of A.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: A man walks 15 m towards the west, turns right and walks 12 m, turns right again and walks 15 m, then turns left and walks 6 m. How far is he from the starting point and in which direction?
questions.explanation_en: West 15 gives (-15, 0); right (north) 12 gives (-15, 12); right (east) 15 gives (0, 12); left (north) 6 gives (0, 18). The east-west displacement cancels, leaving 18 m due north.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: In the evening, just before sunset, Rekha and Sohan stand facing each other. Rekha's shadow falls exactly to her left. In which direction is Sohan facing?
questions.explanation_en: Before sunset the sun is in the west, so shadows fall to the east. East is on Rekha's left, so Rekha faces south. Sohan faces Rekha, so he faces north.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Rohan ranks 12th from the top in a class of 40 students. What is his rank from the bottom?
questions.explanation_en: Rank from bottom = total - rank from top + 1 = 40 - 12 + 1 = 29.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: In a row of girls, Neha is 7th from the left end and 12th from the right end. How many girls are there in the row?
questions.explanation_en: Total = 7 + 12 - 1 = 18 (Neha is counted in both ranks).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: In a row of 40 students, Aman is 14th from the left and Bharat is 18th from the right. How many students are between them?
questions.explanation_en: Bharat's position from the left = 40 - 18 + 1 = 23. Students between = 23 - 14 - 1 = 8.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: A is taller than B, B is taller than C, D is taller than A, and E is shorter than C. Who is the second tallest?
questions.explanation_en: The order is D > A > B > C > E. D is the tallest, so A is second tallest.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Raj is 9th from the top in a class. Amit is 14th from the bottom. If they exchange positions, Raj becomes 19th from the top. How many students are in the class?
questions.explanation_en: Raj now stands where Amit stood, so Amit's original position is 19th from the top and 14th from the bottom. Total = 19 + 14 - 1 = 32.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: P is heavier than Q but lighter than R. S is heavier than R. T is lighter than Q. Who is the second heaviest?
questions.explanation_en: Order from heaviest: S > R > P > Q > T. So R is second heaviest.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Kiran ranks 15th from the top and 25th from the bottom in a class. Divya ranks 7 places above Kiran. What is Divya's rank from the bottom?
questions.explanation_en: Total = 15 + 25 - 1 = 39. Divya's rank from top = 15 - 7 = 8. From the bottom = 39 - 8 + 1 = 32.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: In a row of children facing north, Asha is 18th from the left end and Bina is 21st from the right end. When they interchange their places, Asha becomes 26th from the left end. How many children are there in the row?
questions.explanation_en: After the exchange Asha stands at Bina's old place, so that place is 26th from the left and 21st from the right. Total = 26 + 21 − 1 = 46.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: In a class of 42 students, Tarun is 17th from the top and is 5 places below his friend Sameer. What is Sameer's rank from the bottom?
questions.explanation_en: Sameer is 5 places above Tarun: 17 − 5 = 12th from the top. From the bottom = 42 − 12 + 1 = 31st. 26th is Tarun's rank from the bottom.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Six friends J, K, L, M, N and O are of different ages. L is older than only O. J is older than K but younger than M. N is younger than K but older than L. Who is the third oldest?
questions.explanation_en: L is older than only O, so O is youngest and L second youngest. N > L, K > N, J > K and M > J give M > J > K > N > L > O. The third oldest is K.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: Seven people A, B, C, D, E, F and G sit in a row facing north. C sits at the extreme left end and D at the extreme right end. E sits third to the right of C. B sits between E and G and is an immediate neighbour of both. G sits to the left of E. A sits to the immediate right of E. Who sits between A and D?
questions.explanation_en: C = 1 and D = 7. E is third to the right of C, so E = 4. G is left of E and B sits between them, so B = 3 and G = 2. A = 5 (immediate right of E), which leaves F = 6, the seat between A and D.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 3:30?

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: What is the angle between the hour hand and the minute hand at 4:20?

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: At what time between 4 and 5 o'clock will the two hands of a clock coincide?
questions.explanation_en: Hands coincide when M = (60 × H) / 11 minutes past H. For H = 4: 240/11 = 21 9/11 minutes past 4.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: A watch gains 2 minutes every hour. It was set right at 6:00 a.m. on Monday. What time will it show at the true time of 6:00 p.m. on the same day?
questions.explanation_en: From 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. is 12 hours. Gain = 12 × 2 = 24 minutes, so the watch shows 6:24 p.m.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: On which day of the week did India become independent on 15 August 1947?
questions.explanation_en: Odd-day method: 1600 years = 0, next 300 years = 1, next 46 years (11 leap years) = 57 days = 1, so 1946 years = 2 odd days. Days from 1 Jan to 15 Aug 1947 = 227 = 3 odd days. Total 5 odd days, and 5 corresponds to Friday (0 = Sunday).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: If 26 January 2026 was a Monday, what day of the week was 15 August 2026?
questions.explanation_en: From 26 January to 15 August 2026 (a non-leap year): remaining days of January 5, February 28, March 31, April 30, May 31, June 30, July 31, plus 15 in August = 201 days. 201 = 28 × 7 + 5, so 5 days after Monday = Saturday.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: How many odd days are there in 200 years?
questions.explanation_en: 100 years have 5 odd days, so 200 years have 10 odd days = 10 − 7 = 3 odd days.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: An arrow initially points North. In step 1 it turns 45° clockwise, in step 2 it turns 90° clockwise, in step 3 it turns 135° clockwise, and in step 4 it turns 180° clockwise. In which direction does it point after step 4?
questions.explanation_en: Total rotation = 45 + 90 + 135 + 180 = 450° clockwise. 450 − 360 = 90° clockwise from North = East.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: A pointer initially points East. In each step it turns 90° anticlockwise. In which direction will it point after 5 steps?
questions.explanation_en: 5 × 90° = 450° anticlockwise. 450 − 360 = 90° anticlockwise from East, which is North.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: A wall clock shows 4:20. What time will its image in a plane mirror (placed vertically beside it) appear to show?
questions.explanation_en: Mirror time = 11:60 − actual time = 11:60 − 4:20 = 7:40.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: The mirror image of a clock shows the time as 9:15. What is the actual time?
questions.explanation_en: Actual time = 11:60 − mirror time = 11:60 − 9:15 = 2:45. The relation works both ways.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Blood Relations, Direction, Ranking, Clock & Calendar
questions.question_en: For which of the following times does the mirror image of a clock show the same time as the actual time?
questions.explanation_en: 11:60 − 6:00 = 5:60 = 6:00, so 6:00 looks unchanged (both hands lie on the vertical axis). 3:00 appears as 9:00, 9:30 as 2:30 and 4:20 as 7:40.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statements: All cats are dogs. All dogs are birds.
Conclusions: I. All cats are birds. II. Some birds are dogs.
questions.explanation_en: Cats lie inside dogs, and dogs lie inside birds, so all cats are birds (I). Since all dogs are birds, at least some birds are dogs (II). Both follow.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statements: Some pens are books. All books are tables.
Conclusions: I. Some pens are tables. II. All pens are tables.
questions.explanation_en: The pens that are books are also tables, so some pens are tables (I). Only some pens are known to be books, so 'all pens are tables' (II) cannot be concluded.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statements: No flower is a stone. All stones are rocks.
Conclusions: I. No flower is a rock. II. Some rocks are not flowers.
questions.explanation_en: Stones are rocks and no stone is a flower, so those rocks (the stones) are not flowers: II follows. A flower may still be a rock that is not a stone, so I does not follow.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statements: All teachers are scholars. Some scholars are doctors.
Conclusions: I. Some teachers are doctors. II. Some doctors are scholars.
questions.explanation_en: 'Some scholars are doctors' converts to 'Some doctors are scholars', so II follows. The doctors may be scholars who are not teachers, so I is not certain.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statements: Some men are kings. No king is a thief.
Conclusions: I. Some men are not thieves. II. No man is a thief.
questions.explanation_en: The men who are kings are not thieves, so some men are not thieves (I). Nothing is known about the other men, so II does not follow.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statements: Some tables are chairs. Some chairs are fans.
Conclusions: I. Some tables are fans. II. No table is a fan.
questions.explanation_en: Two 'some' statements give no definite relation, so neither conclusion follows on its own. But I (Some tables are fans) and II (No table is a fan) are contradictories, exactly one of which must be true, so either I or II follows.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statements: All roses are flowers. All flowers are plants. Some plants are trees.
Conclusions: I. Some plants are roses. II. Some trees are roses.
questions.explanation_en: Roses are inside flowers, which are inside plants, so all roses are plants and hence some plants are roses (I). The trees need not overlap with roses, so II does not follow.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statements: All pencils are pens. No pen is a rubber.
Conclusions: I. No pencil is a rubber. II. No rubber is a pencil.
questions.explanation_en: Pencils lie inside pens, and pens have no overlap with rubbers, so no pencil is a rubber (I). A universal negative converts, so no rubber is a pencil (II).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statement: Ravi scored 95% in Mathematics this year, whereas last year he scored 60%.
Conclusions: I. Ravi worked harder this year. II. Ravi's marks in Mathematics improved this year.
questions.explanation_en: The improvement in marks is stated directly (II). The reason for it (harder work) is an assumption; he could have improved for other reasons, so I does not follow.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statement: The government has increased the tax on cigarettes by 50%.
Conclusions: I. The price of cigarettes is likely to rise. II. Every smoker will quit smoking.
questions.explanation_en: A higher tax raises the cost to sellers, so a price rise is a reasonable conclusion. 'Every smoker will quit' is an extreme claim that cannot be drawn.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statement: All the roads leading to the stadium were blocked after heavy rain.
Conclusions: I. People found it difficult to reach the stadium by road. II. The match was cancelled.
questions.explanation_en: Blocked roads make road access difficult (I). Nothing in the statement says the match was cancelled (II).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statement: Only candidates holding a graduate degree can apply for the post of TGT.
Conclusions: I. A person without a graduate degree cannot apply for the post. II. Every graduate will get the post.
questions.explanation_en: The statement sets a necessary condition, so I follows. Being eligible to apply does not guarantee selection, so II does not follow.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statement: Many students of Class X prefer science to arts.
Conclusions: I. All students of Class X prefer science. II. Some students of Class X prefer science.
questions.explanation_en: 'Many' implies at least some, so II follows. 'All' is too strong, so I does not follow.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statement: In the last election the voter turnout in the city was 62%, compared with 55% five years earlier.
Conclusions: I. A larger share of voters turned out than five years ago. II. The number of voters has doubled.
questions.explanation_en: 62% against 55% shows a higher turnout rate (I). Turnout rates alone say nothing about the doubling of voters (II).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statement: Should plastic bags be banned in India?
Arguments: I. Yes, they cause pollution and clog drains. II. No, because they are cheap.

options.en: Both I and II are strong
Neither I nor II is strong

questions.explanation_en: Environmental damage is a valid and weighty reason (strong). Low cost is not a sufficient reason to keep a harmful item, so II is weak.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statement: Should smoking be banned in public places?
Arguments: I. Yes, passive smoking harms the health of non-smokers. II. No, smokers have the right to smoke anywhere they like.

options.en: Both I and II are strong
Neither I nor II is strong

questions.explanation_en: I gives a strong public-health reason. II claims an unlimited right, which ignores harm to others, so it is weak.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statement: Should online classes completely replace classroom teaching?
Arguments: I. Yes, because they save travel time. II. No, because face-to-face interaction is essential for the social and emotional development of children.

options.en: Both I and II are strong
Neither I nor II is strong

questions.explanation_en: Saving travel time is too minor to justify a complete replacement, so I is weak. Social and emotional development is a weighty educational concern, so II is strong.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statement: Should students be given homework daily?
Arguments: I. Yes, it helps them revise and practise concepts. II. No, because teachers do not like checking it.

options.en: Both I and II are strong
Neither I nor II is strong

questions.explanation_en: Learning value is a valid educational reason (strong). The convenience of teachers is not a good reason against a practice that helps students, so II is weak.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statement: Should the retirement age of teachers be raised?
Arguments: I. Yes, experienced teachers can continue to contribute and ease the shortage of teachers. II. No, it will reduce job opportunities for young graduates.

options.en: Neither I nor II is strong
Both I and II are strong

questions.explanation_en: Each argument raises a real, relevant consequence: teacher shortage and fewer vacancies for the young. Both are strong.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statement: Should school uniforms be abolished?
Arguments: I. Yes, because uniforms are old-fashioned. II. No, because a particular tailor will lose business.

options.en: Neither I nor II is strong
Both I and II are strong

questions.explanation_en: 'Old-fashioned' is a matter of opinion and not a sound reason. The business of one tailor is a narrow, personal concern. Neither argument is strong.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statement: Many people in a colony are suffering from dengue.
Courses of action: I. The municipal corporation should start fogging and remove stagnant water. II. People should be asked to leave the colony permanently.
questions.explanation_en: Fogging and removing breeding sites tackle the cause (I). Asking people to leave permanently is impractical and extreme (II).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statement: The number of road accidents on a highway has increased due to over-speeding.
Courses of action: I. Speed cameras and fines should be introduced. II. The highway should be closed forever.
questions.explanation_en: Speed monitoring and penalties directly address over-speeding. Closing the highway forever is an extreme step.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statement: A large number of students of a school failed in Mathematics in the Class X examination.
Courses of action: I. The school should arrange remedial classes. II. The school should stop teaching Mathematics.
questions.explanation_en: Remedial classes help weak students improve (I). Dropping a compulsory subject is not a solution (II).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statement: A major fire broke out in a market due to a short circuit.
Courses of action: I. A fire-safety audit of the market should be conducted. II. The electrical wiring of the shops should be inspected and repaired.
questions.explanation_en: The cause is faulty wiring, so inspecting the wiring (II) and auditing fire safety to prevent a repeat (I) are both practical and relevant.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statement: Public toilets at the railway station are very dirty.
Courses of action: I. Railway should ask passengers to avoid using them. II. Railway authorities should appoint more cleaners and monitor cleanliness regularly.
questions.explanation_en: Toilets exist to be used, so telling passengers to avoid them does not solve the problem (I). More cleaners and monitoring directly remove the problem (II).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en:
Statement: A survey shows that school students spend more than five hours daily on mobile phones.
Courses of action: I. Parents and teachers should guide students on limited and productive use of mobiles. II. Mobile phones should be completely banned for all citizens.
questions.explanation_en: Guidance targets the problem group in a realistic way (I). A complete ban for all citizens is out of proportion to a problem concerning students (II).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en: Which Venn diagram best represents the relationship among Doctors, Surgeons and Teachers?

options.en: Surgeons lie wholly inside Doctors; Teachers form a separate circle outside both
Three circles overlapping at a common region
Doctors lie inside Surgeons, and Teachers lie inside Doctors

questions.explanation_en: Every surgeon is a doctor, so Surgeons is a subset of Doctors. A teacher is a different profession, so Teachers is a separate set.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en: Which Venn diagram best represents the relationship among Pen, Pencil and Stationery?

options.en: Pen and Pencil as two separate circles, both inside the Stationery circle
Pen and Pencil overlapping each other and outside Stationery

questions.explanation_en: A pen is not a pencil, so they are separate sets, but both are stationery items and so lie inside the larger Stationery set.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en: In a class of 50 students, 30 play cricket, 25 play football and 10 play both. How many students play neither game?
questions.explanation_en: Students playing at least one game = 30 + 25 - 10 = 45. Neither = 50 - 45 = 5.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en: In a group of 100 people, 60 speak Hindi, 45 speak English and 15 speak both. How many speak only English?
questions.explanation_en: Only English = total English - both = 45 - 15 = 30. (45 is the number speaking only Hindi.)

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en: In a survey of 120 students, 70 like tea, 60 like coffee and 30 like both. How many students like exactly one of the two drinks?
questions.explanation_en: Only tea = 70 - 30 = 40; only coffee = 60 - 30 = 30. Exactly one = 40 + 30 = 70.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en: In a class of 60 students, 30 study Physics, 25 Chemistry and 20 Mathematics. 10 study Physics and Chemistry, 8 Chemistry and Mathematics, 6 Physics and Mathematics, and 4 study all three. How many students study at least one of the three subjects?
questions.explanation_en: By inclusion-exclusion: 30 + 25 + 20 - 10 - 8 - 6 + 4 = 55.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en: Which Venn diagram best represents the relationship among Mothers, Sisters and Women?

options.en: Mothers and Sisters as two separate circles, both inside Women
Mothers and Sisters as two partly overlapping circles, both inside the Women circle

questions.explanation_en: All mothers and all sisters are women. A woman can be both a mother and a sister, so the two circles overlap partly inside Women.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en: If + means ×, × means −, − means ÷ and ÷ means +, then the value of 12 + 3 × 5 − 5 ÷ 4 is:
questions.explanation_en: Substitute the real signs: 12 × 3 − 5 ÷ 5 + 4. BODMAS: 12 × 3 = 36 and 5 ÷ 5 = 1, so 36 − 1 + 4 = 39.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en: If P means +, Q means −, R means × and S means ÷, then 20 R 3 P 8 S 4 Q 5 = ?
questions.explanation_en: Replace the letters: 20 × 3 + 8 ÷ 4 − 5. By BODMAS: 60 + 2 − 5 = 57.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en: If + and − are interchanged, and × and ÷ are interchanged, then 24 ÷ 6 + 8 × 2 − 3 = ?
questions.explanation_en: After interchanging the signs the expression is 24 × 6 − 8 ÷ 2 + 3. BODMAS: 144 − 4 + 3 = 143.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en: If the numbers 3 and 5 are interchanged and the signs + and × are interchanged, then the value of 3 + 5 × 4 is:
questions.explanation_en: Interchanging 3 and 5 gives 5 + 3 × 4; interchanging the signs gives 5 × 3 + 4. So 15 + 4 = 19.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.explanation_en: The rule is a # b = a × (b + 1): 2 × 4 = 8, 4 × 6 = 24, 6 × 8 = 48. So 8 × 10 = 80. (72 is 8 × 9, which ignores the +1.)

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en: Select the correct combination of signs to fill the blanks in order: 12 _ 4 _ 3 _ 6 = 15
questions.explanation_en: Test the options with BODMAS: 12 ÷ 4 × 3 + 6 = 3 × 3 + 6 = 15 ✓. The first option gives 12 × 4 ÷ 3 + 6 = 22, the second 12 + 4 ÷ 3 × 6 = 20 and the third 12 ÷ 4 + 3 × 6 = 21.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Syllogism, Statements, Venn Diagrams & Mathematical Operations
questions.question_en: If + means ÷, − means ×, × means + and ÷ means −, then 36 + 9 − 4 × 5 ÷ 3 = ?
questions.explanation_en: Replace the signs: 36 ÷ 9 × 4 + 5 − 3. BODMAS: 36 ÷ 9 = 4, then 4 × 4 = 16, so 16 + 5 − 3 = 18.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A triangle ABC has three straight lines drawn from vertex A to three different points on side BC, so that BC is divided into 4 parts. How many triangles are there in the figure?
questions.explanation_en: There are 5 points on BC (B, the three new points and C). Every pair of points on BC with apex A forms a triangle, so the count is C(5,2) = 10.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: In triangle ABC, three lines are drawn from vertex A to BC dividing BC into 4 parts. A line parallel to BC is then drawn across the triangle, cutting AB, AC and all three inner lines. How many triangles are there now?
questions.explanation_en: With apex A, each horizontal 'base' (BC and the parallel line) has 5 points, giving C(5,2) = 10 triangles each. Total = 2 × 10 = 20. (Only triangles with apex A exist; the strips below the parallel line are trapeziums.)

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A square has both of its diagonals drawn. How many triangles are there in the figure?
questions.explanation_en: The diagonals create 4 small triangles meeting at the centre. Each diagonal also splits the square into 2 large triangles, giving 2 + 2 = 4 more. Total = 4 + 4 = 8.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A square has both its diagonals drawn and also the two lines joining the mid-points of opposite sides. How many triangles are there in the figure?
questions.explanation_en: There are 8 smallest triangles. Pairs of adjacent small triangles form 4 medium triangles (each with a whole side of the square as base), and the two diagonals give 4 large triangles. Total = 8 + 4 + 4 = 16.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: An equilateral triangle has each side divided into 3 equal parts, and lines parallel to the sides are drawn through the division points, forming 9 small triangles. How many triangles are there in all?
questions.explanation_en: Upright triangles: size 1 → 6, size 2 → 3, size 3 → 1 (total 10). Inverted triangles: size 1 → 3. Total = 10 + 3 = 13.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: An equilateral triangle has each side divided into 4 equal parts, and lines parallel to the sides are drawn through the division points, forming 16 small triangles. How many triangles are there in all?
questions.explanation_en: Upright: size 1 → 10, size 2 → 6, size 3 → 3, size 4 → 1 (total 20). Inverted: size 1 → 6, size 2 → 1 (total 7). Total = 20 + 7 = 27.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A large square is divided into a 4 × 4 grid of 16 equal small squares. How many squares of all sizes are there in the figure?
questions.explanation_en: Squares of side k in an n × n grid = (n − k + 1)². For n = 4: 16 + 9 + 4 + 1 = 30. The answer 16 counts only the smallest squares.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A square is divided into a 3 × 3 grid of 9 equal small squares. How many rectangles (including squares) are there in the figure?
questions.explanation_en: A rectangle is fixed by choosing 2 of the 4 vertical lines and 2 of the 4 horizontal lines: C(4,2) × C(4,2) = 6 × 6 = 36. The answer 14 counts only squares (9 + 4 + 1).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: How many squares of all sizes are there on a standard 8 × 8 chessboard?
questions.explanation_en: Total = 1² + 2² + … + 8² = 8 × 9 × 17 / 6 = 204. 64 counts only the unit squares.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: The vertices of a regular octagon are numbered 1 to 8 clockwise. In a series of figures a star sits on vertices 1, 2, 4, 7, … (it moves 1, 2, 3, … places clockwise). On which vertex will it be in the fifth figure?
questions.explanation_en: From 7 it moves 4 places: 7 + 4 = 11, and 11 − 8 = 3. So the star is on vertex 3.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: The corners of a square carry letters: top-left A, top-right B, bottom-right C, bottom-left D. In every step, each letter moves one corner clockwise. After 3 steps, which letter is at the top-left corner?
questions.explanation_en: Moving clockwise, the top-left corner receives the letter from bottom-left each step: after step 1 it has D, after step 2 C, after step 3 B.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A row has 5 boxes numbered 1 to 5. In figure 1, box 1 is shaded. In each next figure the shading moves 2 boxes to the right, returning to the start after box 5 (box 5 → box 2). Which box is shaded in figure 6?
questions.explanation_en: Figures 1 to 6: box 1 → 3 → 5 → 2 → 4 → 1. So in figure 6 box 1 is shaded.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: Three different positions of the same die show these numbers on the three visible (mutually adjacent) faces — Position 1: 1, 2, 3; Position 2: 1, 3, 6; Position 3: 1, 6, 5. Which number is on the face opposite 1?
questions.explanation_en: 1 appears with 2, 3, 6 and 5, so these four are all adjacent to 1. The only number never seen with 1 is 4, so 4 is opposite 1.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A standard die (opposite faces add up to 7) rests on a table with 3 on the top face. What is the sum of the numbers on the four vertical side faces?
questions.explanation_en: Total of all faces = 1 + 2 + … + 6 = 21. Top 3 and bottom 4 (opposite of 3) add to 7, so the four sides add to 21 − 7 = 14. The sides of a standard die always total 14.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A standard die (opposite faces add up to 7) shows 1 on top, 2 facing you (front) and 3 on the right. It is rolled one quarter-turn to the right, so that the top face goes to the right side. Which number is now on top?
questions.explanation_en: When a die rolls to the right, the left face comes to the top. Left is opposite right (3), so left = 7 − 3 = 4. Hence 4 is on top.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A cube is folded from a net made of six squares: four squares A, B, C, D in a horizontal row (left to right), with square E attached above B and square F attached below B. Which face is opposite A?
questions.explanation_en: In a row of four squares that wraps around the cube, alternate squares are opposite: A–C and B–D. E and F, attached on either side of the row, become top and bottom and are opposite each other.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A cube net has four squares P, Q, R, S in a horizontal row (left to right), square T attached above P and square U attached below S. When folded into a cube, which face is opposite T?
questions.explanation_en: The row P–Q–R–S wraps around the cube, so P–R and Q–S are opposite. The two squares attached off the row (T and U) form the two remaining faces, which are opposite each other, whichever row square they are attached to.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: Two positions of the same die are described. Position 1: 2 on top, 5 in front, 1 on the right. Position 2: 2 on top, 6 in front, 3 on the right. Which number is opposite 5?
questions.explanation_en: 2 stays on top in both positions, so the die has only been turned about the vertical axis. A quarter turn would bring 1 (the old right face) or the old left face to the front, but 6 is now in front and 3 on the right, so the turn was 180°. Hence the back face is 6 (opposite front 5) and the left face is 3 (opposite 1).

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A cube net has two rows of three squares. The upper row has squares 1, 2, 3 from left to right. The lower row has squares 4, 5, 6 from left to right, with square 4 directly below square 3 (so the lower row continues to the right). Which number is opposite 2 when the cube is folded?
questions.explanation_en: In a straight run of three squares the end squares are opposite: 1–3 in the upper row and 4–6 in the lower row. The two middle squares, 2 and 5, are left and must be opposite each other.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: Two positions of the same die are described. Position 1: 4 on top, 5 in front, 6 on the right. Position 2: 6 on top, 1 in front, 4 on the right. Which number is opposite 5?
questions.explanation_en: With 4 on top, the side faces form a ring 5 (front), 6 (right), back, left. Position 2 shows 1 touching both 4 and 6, so 1 is a ring-neighbour of 6. The ring-neighbours of 6 are the front (5) and the back; 1 is not 5, so 1 is at the back, i.e. opposite 5.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A cube is painted on all six faces and then cut into 64 identical smaller cubes. How many small cubes have exactly two faces painted?
questions.explanation_en: 64 = 4³, so n = 4. Cubes with exactly two painted faces lie on the 12 edges, excluding corners: 12 × (n − 2) = 12 × 2 = 24.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A cube painted on all faces is cut into 125 identical smaller cubes. How many small cubes have exactly one face painted?
questions.explanation_en: 125 = 5³, n = 5. One-face cubes are the inner part of each face: 6 × (n − 2)² = 6 × 9 = 54. 36 is the two-face count 12 × 3; 27 is the unpainted count 3³.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A cube painted on all faces is cut into 216 identical smaller cubes. How many small cubes have no face painted?
questions.explanation_en: 216 = 6³, n = 6. Unpainted cubes form the inner core of side n − 2 = 4, so 4³ = 64. 96 is the one-face count 6 × 4².

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A painted cube is cut into identical smaller cubes. Exactly 96 of the small cubes have only one face painted. How many small cubes have exactly two faces painted?
questions.explanation_en: 6(n − 2)² = 96 gives (n − 2)² = 16, so n − 2 = 4 and n = 6. Two-face cubes = 12 × (n − 2) = 12 × 4 = 48.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A cube has two opposite faces painted red, two opposite faces painted green and the remaining two faces painted blue. It is cut into 125 identical small cubes. How many small cubes have only red and green paint (one face of each, no blue)?
questions.explanation_en: Each red face meets each green face along one edge: 2 × 2 = 4 red–green edges. Excluding the corner cubes (which also have blue), each edge has n − 2 = 3 cubes, so 4 × 3 = 12.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A cube has two opposite faces painted red, two opposite faces green and two opposite faces blue. It is cut into 64 identical small cubes. How many small cubes have exactly one face painted, that face being red?
questions.explanation_en: Each face has (n − 2)² = 2² = 4 cubes with only that face painted. There are 2 red faces, so 2 × 4 = 8.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A wooden cube has only its four vertical side faces painted (top and bottom are left unpainted). It is cut into 27 identical small cubes. How many small cubes have no paint at all?
questions.explanation_en: In the 3 × 3 top view, only the centre column is away from all four painted sides. That column contains 3 cubes (one per layer), and since the top and bottom are unpainted, all 3 are paint-free. Answer 1 would be the case if all six faces were painted.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A cuboid of size 4 cm × 3 cm × 2 cm is painted on all faces and cut into 1 cm cubes. How many cubes have exactly one face painted?
questions.explanation_en: One-face cubes on an a × b face = (a − 2)(b − 2). The 4 × 3 faces give 2 × 1 = 2 each (two faces → 4); the 4 × 2 and 3 × 2 faces give 0 because 2 − 2 = 0. Total = 4.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: What is the minimum number of straight cuts needed to divide a cube into 64 identical smaller cubes?
questions.explanation_en: 64 = 4 × 4 × 4 pieces need 3 cuts in each of the three directions: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: Which word will look exactly the same when seen in a vertical mirror placed to its right?
questions.explanation_en: A vertical mirror reverses the letter order and flips each letter left–right. MOM is a palindrome made only of letters symmetric about a vertical axis (M, O). D, N and B are not vertically symmetric, so their images look reversed.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: Which word will look exactly the same in its water image (reflection in water below the word)?
questions.explanation_en: A water image keeps the letter order but flips each letter top-to-bottom. All letters of CHOICE (C, H, O, I, E) are symmetric about a horizontal axis. R, V, P, L, M, U, S are not.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: How many letters of the word EXAMINATION (counting repeated letters each time) look the same in a vertical mirror?
questions.explanation_en: Vertically symmetric letters: X, A, M, I, A, T, I, O = 8. E and the two Ns are not symmetric about a vertical axis.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A square sheet of paper is folded in half, and then folded in half again to form a smaller square. One hole is punched through all the layers. How many holes will there be when the sheet is unfolded?
questions.explanation_en: Two folds make 2 × 2 = 4 layers, and a hole punched through all layers appears once in each layer. So 4 holes.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A square sheet is folded along one diagonal to form a triangle, and this triangle is folded in half again to form a smaller triangle. A single hole is punched through it. How many holes are seen on unfolding?
questions.explanation_en: Each fold doubles the layers: 2 folds → 4 layers, so one punch gives 4 holes, placed symmetrically about both diagonals.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A rectangular sheet is folded in half. A semicircle is cut out from the middle of the folded edge (the curved side pointing away from the fold). What will the sheet look like when unfolded?

options.en: Two semicircular holes at the outer edges
One circular hole in the middle of the sheet
Two circular holes side by side
One semicircular notch on the outer edge

questions.explanation_en: The cut is made on the fold line, so its mirror image joins it across the fold: two halves of a circle meet to form one complete circular hole in the middle.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A rectangular sheet is folded in half. A small triangular notch is cut from the folded edge, with the base of the triangle lying on the fold. What will be seen on unfolding?

options.en: A triangular hole near the edge
A square notch at one corner
A diamond (rhombus) shaped hole on the fold line

questions.explanation_en: The triangle and its mirror image across the fold share the base, so together they form a diamond-shaped (rhombus) hole centred on the fold line.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A square sheet of side 16 cm is folded in half along a vertical line, then in half along a horizontal line, and then again in half along a vertical line. What are the dimensions of the folded paper?
questions.explanation_en: 16 × 16 → vertical fold → 8 (wide) × 16 (high) → horizontal fold → 8 × 8 → vertical fold → 4 × 8. Area check: 256 / 8 layers = 32 = 4 × 8.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A square sheet is folded once along its vertical centre line so that the right half lies on the left half. A hole is punched near the top-left corner of the folded sheet. On unfolding, where will the holes be?

options.en: Near the top-left and bottom-left corners
Near the top-left and top-right corners

questions.explanation_en: The hole goes through both layers. The right half is the mirror image of the left half about the vertical fold, so the second hole appears near the top-right corner.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A square sheet is folded top-half onto bottom-half, and then right-half onto left-half, giving a smaller square. A quarter-circle is cut from the corner of this small square where the two fold lines meet. What will the sheet look like when unfolded?

options.en: Four quarter-circle notches at the corners
Two semicircular notches on opposite edges
Four small circular holes near the centre
One circular hole at the centre of the sheet

questions.explanation_en: The corner where both folds meet is the centre of the original sheet. The four quarter-circles (one in each layer) meet at that point and form a single circle, giving one circular hole at the centre.

questions.chapter: General Intelligence & Reasoning — Non-verbal Reasoning (Figures, Dice, Cubes, Paper Folding)
questions.question_en: A square sheet is folded top-half onto bottom-half, and then right-half onto left-half. A small triangle is cut off at the corner of the folded square that is diagonally opposite to the corner where the two fold lines meet. What will the sheet look like when unfolded?

options.en: All four corners of the sheet are cut off
Only one corner of the sheet is cut off
Two adjacent corners are cut off
A diamond-shaped hole appears at the centre

questions.explanation_en: The fold-line corner is the centre of the sheet, so the opposite corner of the folded square holds all four original corners stacked together. One cut therefore removes all four corners of the sheet.
